Unit verification. 1. It keeps the attention in the story: "Here it is," "then" (or nothing). · 2. Introduces an explanation or justification: the fact is that it is. · 3. Nearest: "Let's say" · 4. Egyptian grammar with the vocabulary of fuṣḥā, used by people educated on technical or public topics: il-mawḍūʿ from miḥtāg tadaḫḫul sarīʿ. · 9. The faithful contains everything (hearings, repetitions, self-corrections, laughter); cleanness contains the words of the speaker without hesitation or unnecessary repetitions. · 10. At most two lines of about 40 characters; one to six seconds; a unity of sense; hesitations and discursive signals are cut; names, numbers and denials do not touch each other. Integral translation: "Guardi," I worked in tourism for ten years. The point is that tourism is not only monuments and hotels: tourism are people. And it's not over: there are tourists who come especially to eat koshari in the center! The problem is that sometimes we think only of numbers, the number of tourists and the money, and let's forget that the tourist, when he comes back to his country, will tell about the people he met, not the hotel. And this, as I said, is the most important advertising for Egypt. □ Example subtitles: □ I have worked ten years in tourism. / Tourism is not only monuments: • Tourism are people. • Evaluation: transcription 4 (one point less every three errors of speech or incoherent spelling), translation 3, subtitles 3 (Length, cuts, sense).
